c1-gen-0057: Cain was scared of what might happen to him out there. Let's read Genesis 4:15 together.
c1-gen-0058: Families traveled a long way from the east, looking for a place to settle. Genesis 11:2 says where they stopped.
c2-gen-0004: Cain was angry and frowning. Listen closely as the LORD speaks in Genesis 4:6 and Genesis 4:7.
c2-gen-0005: The LORD asked Cain a question, and Cain gave a hard reply. Hear it for yourself in Genesis 4:9.
c2-gen-0006: The ground would not grow crops well for Cain anymore. Keep going in Genesis 4:12 to hear the rest of the LORD's words.
c2-gen-0007: Brick by brick, the builders made big plans. Genesis 11:4 lets us hear what they said to each other.
c2-gen-0008: The LORD came down to see the city and its tower. Look at Genesis 11:7 and Genesis 11:9 one after the other.
c2-gen-0009: Two brothers each brought something to the LORD. Compare Genesis 4:2 with Genesis 4:4, side by side.
c1-gen-0059: Jacob was alone on a long trip, and he lay down to sleep. Genesis 28:12 holds what came next.
c1-gen-0060: All through the night Jacob held on, tired and sore. A big change comes in Genesis 32:28.
c2-gen-0010: Rebekah felt her babies pushing inside her and wondered why. Hear the LORD's answer in Genesis 25:22 and Genesis 25:23.
c2-gen-0011: Esau came in from the field, very hungry, and the stew was ready. See how it all turned out in Genesis 25:32 and Genesis 25:34.
c2-gen-0012: Old Isaac could not see well, so he reached out to feel. Read Genesis 27:22 and Genesis 27:23 with care.
c2-gen-0013: Jacob bowed down again and again, nervous about meeting his brother. Genesis 33:3 and Genesis 33:4 bring us right to that moment.
c2-gen-0014: Morning came at that quiet place where Jacob had slept. Find out what he did in Genesis 28:11 and Genesis 28:18.
c2-gen-0015: Day was coming, and Jacob still would not let go. Keep close to him through Genesis 32:26 and Genesis 32:29.
c1-exo-0017: God picked a skilled builder for the tabernacle work. Meet him in Exodus 31:2 and Exodus 31:3.
c1-exo-0018: Moses heard God's plan for a sanctuary. Exodus 25:8 gives the reason in a few short words.
c2-exo-0002: Cloth, wood, and metal were needed for God's sanctuary. Exodus 25:2 has Moses' instructions.
c2-exo-0003: The workers came to Moses with news from the building site. Their report is in Exodus 36:5 and Exodus 36:6.
c2-exo-0004: Skilled women joined in to help with the tabernacle. Let's look at their work in Exodus 35:25 and Exodus 35:26.
c2-exo-0005: The work was all done, and Moses stood outside. Read Exodus 40:34 and Exodus 40:35 to learn why he could not go in.
c2-exo-0006: A second worker, from the tribe of Dan, was chosen to help. Both Exodus 31:6 and Exodus 35:34 mention him.
c2-exo-0007: Day after day, God's people moved from place to place across the wild land. Think about the whole trip in Exodus 40:34 and Exodus 40:38.
c1-lev-0001: Old hurts can make people want to get even. Leviticus 19:18 says what to do instead.
c1-lev-0002: For seven days each year, families kept a feast. Find where they lived that week in Leviticus 23:42.
c2-lev-0001: Behind the curtain was a room set apart for the LORD. Hear what the LORD told Aaron about it in Leviticus 16:2.
c2-lev-0002: Busy workers were out in the fields and vineyards. Read Leviticus 19:9 and Leviticus 19:10 to see who else was on God's mind.
c2-lev-0003: This verse is about caring for people who cannot hear or see. Let's look at Leviticus 19:14 together.
c2-lev-0004: The land was theirs now, and the crops were ready to cut. Leviticus 23:10 and Leviticus 23:11 explain what to bring.
c2-lev-0005: Aaron placed both hands on the goat's head and spoke. Follow that goat through Leviticus 16:21 and Leviticus 16:22.
c2-lev-0006: Once each year, a very serious day came for God's people. Check the calendar in Leviticus 16:29 and Leviticus 23:27.
c1-num-0001: The spies crept quietly through the land and found a valley. See what two men carried out in Numbers 13:23.
c1-num-0002: Most of the spies came back frightened. Hear their report in Numbers 13:33.
c2-num-0002: Two spies stood up while the whole crowd was upset. Numbers 14:9 gives their reason.
c2-num-0003: Caleb had walked through the land himself. Numbers 14:24 records what the LORD said about him.
c2-num-0004: Thirsty people crowded around Moses at Kadesh. Read the LORD's instructions in Numbers 20:8.
c2-num-0005: Snakes came into the camp, and people were hurting. Numbers 21:5 and Numbers 21:7 have what they said to Moses then.
c2-num-0006: The rock gave plenty for everyone, yet the LORD had hard words for Moses and Aaron. Numbers 20:11 and Numbers 20:12 explain why.
c2-num-0007: A donkey kept stopping on a narrow road. Follow Balaam's trip in Numbers 22:28 and Numbers 22:31.
c1-exo-0019: At Marah the people were thirsty and upset. Exodus 15:23 and Exodus 15:25 describe what the LORD pointed out.
c1-exo-0020: The sun went down over a hungry camp. Find out what arrived in Exodus 16:13.
c2-exo-0008: Morning came, and something small covered the ground. Hear the people talking in Exodus 16:14 and Exodus 16:15.
c2-exo-0009: Some people kept extra for the next day anyway. Read what happened in Exodus 16:19 and Exodus 16:20.
c2-exo-0010: At Rephidim the people were thirsty and arguing. Exodus 17:7 holds the question they asked.
c2-exo-0011: After the battle, Moses built an altar. Exodus 17:15 records what he called it.
c2-exo-0012: On the sixth morning, families went out with their baskets. Count along in Exodus 16:22 and Exodus 16:29.
c2-exo-0013: Down below the battle went on, and Moses grew so tired. Let's read Exodus 17:11 and Exodus 17:12.
c1-deu-0001: Moses was very old as he went up from the plains of Moab. Deuteronomy 34:1 names the place.
c1-deu-0002: The people were sad without Moses, but it was time to move ahead. Read Deuteronomy 34:9 to meet the next leader.
c2-deu-0001: Moses reminded the crowd about the day at Mount Horeb. Hear him speak in Deuteronomy 5:2 and Deuteronomy 5:3.
c2-deu-0002: One special day each week had a reason behind it. Deuteronomy 5:15 asks the people to think back.
c2-deu-0003: Moses told parents to share God's commands over and over. Deuteronomy 6:6 and Deuteronomy 6:7 hold his list.
c2-deu-0004: Moses said no one had to travel far or climb to the sky for it. Deuteronomy 30:12, Deuteronomy 30:13, and Deuteronomy 30:14 complete the thought.
c2-deu-0005: Two ways were set before the people, and heaven and earth were called to listen. Read Deuteronomy 30:15 and Deuteronomy 30:19 for Moses' plea.
c2-deu-0006: Two verses far apart use the very same words. Put Deuteronomy 5:4 beside Deuteronomy 34:10 and compare.
c1-deu-0003: Moses began his long goodbye talk by thinking about the road behind them. Deuteronomy 1:2 measures the trip.
c1-deu-0004: The Jordan was right ahead, and Moses knew he would not cross it. Hear what he said about himself in Deuteronomy 31:2.
c2-deu-0007: Moses looked back on all those years in the wild places. Deuteronomy 1:31 paints a picture worth seeing.
c2-deu-0008: Forty long years of walking in the wilderness. Look closely at Deuteronomy 8:4 for a detail you might not expect.
c2-deu-0009: Moses warned the people not to brag about what they had. Moses' warning goes on in Deuteronomy 8:17 and Deuteronomy 8:18.
c2-deu-0010: Moses spoke about people who are often left out. Deuteronomy 10:18 and Deuteronomy 10:19 give his reason.
c2-deu-0011: Not one of that group would go into the land. Deuteronomy 1:35 and Deuteronomy 1:39 make clear who would.
c2-deu-0012: Moses said the same thing twice, once to everyone and once to the man taking over. Hear both in Deuteronomy 31:6 and Deuteronomy 31:8.
c1-2ki-0001: Naaman was important in Syria, yet he was sick. 2 Kings 5:1 introduces him.
c1-2ki-0002: Elijah and Elisha had crossed the Jordan together. Hear Elisha's request in 2 Kings 2:9.
c2-2ki-0001: The widow kept pouring while her son watched. 2 Kings 4:6 has what he said.
c2-2ki-0002: Elisha often passed through Shunem on his travels. A woman there had an idea in 2 Kings 4:9 and 2 Kings 4:10.
c2-2ki-0003: Naaman stomped off, angry and upset. Then his servants spoke up in 2 Kings 5:13.
c2-2ki-0004: Syrian soldiers surrounded the city, and the servant was scared. Read 2 Kings 6:17 to find what was on the mountain.
c2-2ki-0005: Elisha stood at the river holding Elijah's cloak. Read 2 Kings 2:8, then 2 Kings 2:14.
c2-2ki-0006: Instead of a fight, the captured soldiers were fed and sent away. 2 Kings 6:22 and 2 Kings 6:23 carry the story on.
c1-1ki-0015: King Ahab married Jezebel from Sidon, and things went wrong. 1 Kings 16:31 names the god he followed.
c1-1ki-0016: Naboth's vines grew right beside the king's palace. Hear Ahab's plan in 1 Kings 21:2.
c2-1ki-0003: Naboth gave the king a firm no. 1 Kings 21:3 holds his words.
c2-1ki-0004: Ahab lay on his bed, pouting and grumpy. 1 Kings 21:4 adds one more detail.
c2-1ki-0005: Jezebel wrote letters and pressed the king's seal on them. Find where they went in 1 Kings 21:8.
c2-1ki-0006: Elijah walked into the vineyard where Ahab stood. Ahab's greeting is in 1 Kings 21:20.
c2-1ki-0007: Two men sat in front of Naboth to speak against him. Their claim is written in 1 Kings 21:10 and 1 Kings 21:13.
c2-1ki-0008: Ahab put on rough sackcloth and walked around quietly. See how the LORD answered in 1 Kings 21:27 and 1 Kings 21:29.
c1-2ki-0003: Hezekiah smashed an old bronze statue into pieces. 2 Kings 18:4 says what people had called it.
c1-2ki-0004: Hezekiah was very sick, and he called out to the LORD. The LORD's answer comes in 2 Kings 20:6.
c2-2ki-0007: A loud officer stood outside the city, mocking God's people. Hear his taunt in 2 Kings 18:21.
c2-2ki-0008: The people on the wall heard every mean word. 2 Kings 18:36 explains why nobody answered.
c2-2ki-0009: Hezekiah was offered a sign on the sundial. Read 2 Kings 20:10 and 2 Kings 20:11 to learn his choice.
c2-2ki-0010: Hezekiah turned toward the wall and talked to the LORD. Hear the reply in 2 Kings 20:3 and 2 Kings 20:5.
c2-2ki-0011: A proud king had made big threats against Hezekiah. 2 Kings 19:6, 2 Kings 19:7, and 2 Kings 19:36 trace where he ended up.
c2-2ki-0012: Hezekiah spread the scary letter out before the LORD. His prayer fills 2 Kings 19:14 and 2 Kings 19:19.
c1-1ki-0017: Ahijah tore his coat into twelve pieces as Jeroboam watched. Count with them in 1 Kings 11:30 and 1 Kings 11:31.
c1-2ki-0005: Samaria was surrounded for three long years. 2 Kings 17:6 says where the people were taken.
c2-1ki-0009: The older men gave young King Rehoboam their advice. 1 Kings 12:7 holds it.
c2-1ki-0010: The king spoke roughly, and the crowd grew upset. Their shout rings out in 1 Kings 12:16.
c2-2ki-0013: Smoke rose over the city on a very sad day. Read 2 Kings 25:9 to learn what burned before the rest.
c2-2ki-0014: Most people were led away, but a few poor ones were left behind. 2 Kings 25:12 explains their job.
c2-1ki-0011: Jeroboam was worried about where the people would go to worship. Follow his plan in 1 Kings 12:27, 1 Kings 12:28, and 1 Kings 12:30.
c2-2ki-0015: Prophet after prophet carried the same message. Read 2 Kings 17:13 and 2 Kings 17:14 for what followed.
c1-job-0001: Before anything else happens, we meet a man named Job. Job 1:1 says where he lived.
c1-job-0002: Three friends heard the bad news and set out to be with Job. Job 2:11 lists who they were.
c2-job-0001: In heaven, the LORD spoke about His servant Job. Satan's reply is waiting in Job 1:8 and Job 1:9.
c2-job-0002: Messengers arrived one after another with bad news. See what Job did next in Job 1:20.
c2-job-0003: Seven days and seven nights went by on the ground beside Job. Job 2:13 explains the silence.
c2-job-0004: Job wished his words could be carved in rock forever. Read Job 19:23 and Job 19:25 to complete his sentence.
c2-job-0005: The wind roared as the LORD answered Job. Set Job 38:1 next to Job 42:5.
c2-job-0006: Job's friends came to him with an offering in hand. Job 42:8 and Job 42:10 say when things changed.
c1-job-0003: After a long silence, Job finally spoke up. Job 3:1 is where his words begin.
c1-job-0004: The LORD asked Job big questions, and Job felt very small. Read Job 40:3 and Job 40:4 for his answer.
c2-job-0007: Job's sadness came out in honest words. Job 3:25 and Job 3:26 are the place to look.
c2-job-0008: Job spoke four strong words: though He slay me. Job 13:15 carries them further.
c2-job-0009: Job still felt bitter, and he had a big wish. Job 23:3 puts it into words.
c2-job-0010: The LORD pointed Job toward a huge animal called behemoth. Read Job 40:15 to learn about it.
c2-job-0011: Job searched in every direction, front, back, left, and right. Job 23:8, Job 23:9, and Job 23:10 complete his thought.
c2-job-0012: Could anyone catch Leviathan with a fishhook? Listen to the LORD in Job 41:1, Job 41:10, and Job 41:11.
c1-isa-0002: Isaiah remembered the year everything changed for him. Isaiah 6:1 begins with that year.
c1-isa-0003: Each seraph had six wings, and their voices filled the place. Hear them call out in Isaiah 6:2 and Isaiah 6:3.
c2-isa-0001: Isaiah cried out, sure he could not stand before God. Isaiah 6:5, Isaiah 6:6, and Isaiah 6:7 describe what the seraph did.
c2-isa-0002: The Lord asked a question, and Isaiah heard it. Isaiah 6:8 holds his reply.
c2-isa-0003: Grass dries up and flowers fade, Isaiah says. Isaiah 40:7 and Isaiah 40:8 point to what lasts.
c2-isa-0004: Everyone feels afraid sometimes. Hear what God said to His people in Isaiah 43:1 and Isaiah 43:2.
c2-isa-0005: Even strong young people trip and fall sometimes. Isaiah 40:28, Isaiah 40:30, and Isaiah 40:31 paint a picture to remember.
c2-isa-0006: Rain and snow come down and soak the earth. Read Isaiah 55:10 and Isaiah 55:11 and hear what God says.
c1-isa-0004: A sign was coming, Isaiah said, a baby boy. Isaiah 7:14 gives what He will be called.
c1-isa-0005: The LORD invited a king to ask for any sign at all, deep or high. Isaiah 7:10, Isaiah 7:11, and Isaiah 7:12 identify the king.
c2-isa-0007: Picture people walking in deep darkness. Isaiah 9:2 says what they have seen.
c2-isa-0008: A Child is born, Isaiah says, with a big job on His shoulders. Isaiah 9:6 lists what He will be called.
c2-isa-0009: Wild animals and gentle ones lying down side by side. Isaiah 11:6 completes the picture.
c2-isa-0010: Isaiah looked ahead to how God's Servant would grow up. Isaiah 53:2 describes it.
c2-isa-0011: Isaiah speaks of a Rod from Jesse's family. Read Isaiah 11:1 and Isaiah 11:10 to see what He will be for the people.
c2-isa-0012: Isaiah wrote a long and sad passage about God's Servant. Isaiah 52:13 starts it, and Isaiah 53:12 closes it.
c1-psa-0016: Trumpets, harps, and cymbals fill this song with sound. Read Psalm 150:3 and Psalm 150:6 to hear its closing call.
c1-psa-0017: Travelers sang this song as they climbed toward the city. Psalm 122:6 gives them something to ask for.
c2-psa-0002: Who may climb the hill of the LORD? Psalm 24:3 asks, and Psalm 24:4 answers.
c2-psa-0003: Thunder rumbles through this song about the voice of the LORD. Psalm 29:4 and Psalm 29:5 say what it can do.
c2-psa-0004: One day in God's courts beats a thousand anywhere else, the writer says. Psalm 84:10 goes on from there.
c2-psa-0005: Come, let us bow down, this song begins. Psalm 95:6 and Psalm 95:7 give the reason.
c2-psa-0006: This song praises the LORD's teaching as perfect. Psalm 19:7 and Psalm 19:10 hold two comparisons.
c2-psa-0007: Under a sky full of stars, the writer feels very small. Psalm 8:4 and Psalm 8:5 hold his answer.
c1-pro-0016: A lazy person is sent outside to learn a lesson. Proverbs 6:6 points the way.
c1-pro-0017: Money passes from one person to another in this proverb. Think about what Proverbs 22:7 says.
c2-pro-0002: Back to that small creature storing up for later. Proverbs 6:7 and Proverbs 6:8 describe how it works.
c2-pro-0003: Two kinds of hands appear side by side in this proverb. Proverbs 10:4 compares them.
c2-pro-0004: One person gives freely, and another holds on tight. Proverbs 11:24 and Proverbs 11:25 compare what happens to each.
c2-pro-0005: Having only a little, but doing what is right. Proverbs 16:8 completes the comparison.
c2-pro-0006: A little sleep, a little nap, the proverb warns. Proverbs 6:10, Proverbs 6:11, and Proverbs 10:5 picture two sons out in the fields.
c2-pro-0007: Money can come and go quickly, these proverbs warn. Proverbs 11:28 and Proverbs 13:11 say what happens next.
c1-mat-0031: A farmer planted good seed, and everyone went to sleep. Read Matthew 13:24 and Matthew 13:25 to see who slipped in.
c1-mat-0032: Peter asked Jesus a question about forgiving. Matthew 18:21 and Matthew 18:22 carry Jesus' answer.
c2-mat-0001: Weeds and wheat were growing in the same field. Matthew 13:29 and Matthew 13:30 give the owner's plan.
c2-mat-0002: A man stumbled on something hidden in a field. Matthew 13:44 says why he sold everything.
c2-mat-0003: A servant was let off a huge debt, then met a coworker who owed him. Matthew 18:24 and Matthew 18:28 give the amounts.
c2-mat-0004: Ten young women waited with lamps for the bridegroom. Matthew 25:3 and Matthew 25:4 point out the difference.
c2-mat-0005: The master came back and looked over what his servants had done. Read Matthew 25:21 and Matthew 25:23 for his words.
c2-luk-0002: A wide gap separated the rich man from Abraham. Luke 16:26, Luke 16:29, and Luke 16:31 hold their talk.
c1-jhn-0029: Nicodemus was an important teacher who wanted to talk with Jesus. John 3:1 and John 3:2 say when he came.
c1-jhn-0030: Jesus was tired and dusty from walking through Samaria. Find where He sat in John 4:5 and John 4:6.
c2-jhn-0002: Nicodemus came full of questions. Jesus' reply is in John 3:2 and John 3:3.
c2-jhn-0003: The woman was surprised that Jesus spoke to her at all. John 4:9 and John 4:10 have His answer.
c2-jhn-0004: She spoke about a mountain and a city as places to worship. Hear what Jesus said in John 4:23 and John 4:24.
c2-jhn-0005: The woman hurried back into town, excited to share. Look closely at John 4:28 and John 4:29.
c2-jhn-0006: Jesus spoke of people who hide what they do. Read John 3:19 and then John 3:21.
c2-jhn-0007: The townspeople listened to the woman, then heard Jesus for themselves. John 4:39 and John 4:42 hold what they said.
c1-mat-0033: Judas went to the chief priests with a sneaky plan. Matthew 26:14 and Matthew 26:15 record their deal.
c1-mat-0034: The whole city was stirred up, everyone asking the same question. Hear the crowd in Matthew 21:10 and Matthew 21:11.
c2-mat-0006: Tables tipped over and the money changers scrambled. Find the Scripture Jesus quoted in Matthew 21:12 and Matthew 21:13.
c2-mat-0007: The leaders were upset by all the shouting they heard. Jesus answered with old words from the Psalms in Matthew 21:15 and Matthew 21:16.
c2-mat-0008: A crowd with swords and clubs came with Judas to find Jesus. Matthew 26:47 and Matthew 26:48 reveal his signal.
c2-mat-0009: Peter said it a third time: I do not know the Man. Read Matthew 26:74 and Matthew 26:75 for what came right after.
c2-mat-0010: Jesus stood quiet while people shouted charges at Him. Watch the governor in Matthew 26:63 and Matthew 27:14.
c2-mat-0011: Pilate's wife sent a worried message, and later Pilate washed his hands. Matthew 27:19 and Matthew 27:24 use one word for Jesus.
c1-luk-0035: Two followers walked and talked on the road out of town. Luke 24:13 names where they were going.
c1-jhn-0031: Jesus came to His disciples once more, in a different spot. Discover where in John 21:1.
c2-luk-0003: At the table they knew Him, and then He was gone. Luke 24:31 and Luke 24:32 describe how the walk felt.
c2-jhn-0008: Jesus stood with His disciples and sent them out. Listen for His next words in John 20:21 and John 20:22.
c2-jhn-0009: Thomas had doubts, and eight days later Jesus stood before him. Hear his reply in John 20:27 and John 20:28.
c2-act-0003: The disciples had a big question before Jesus went up. Acts 1:6 and Acts 1:7 give His reply.
c2-luk-0004: Jesus gave His friends one more instruction before He was carried up. Luke 24:49, Luke 24:52, and Luke 24:53 show what they did.
c2-jhn-0010: After breakfast, Jesus asked Peter the same question three times. John 21:15 and John 21:17 hold His charge.
c1-act-0029: The leaders at Antioch were busy with the Lord's work. Acts 13:2 and Acts 13:3 name the two who were called.
c1-act-0030: By a quiet river outside Philippi, a small group met to talk with God. Lydia's work is named in Acts 16:13 and Acts 16:14.
c2-act-0004: Paul's team sailed on, but John left them. Follow his path in Acts 13:5 and Acts 13:13.
c2-act-0005: A man who had never walked jumped up, and the crowd went wild. Acts 14:11 and Acts 14:12 explain the names they shouted.
c2-act-0006: In busy Athens, Paul stood up to speak. Read the altar's words in Acts 17:22 and Acts 17:23.
c2-act-0007: Paul met a husband and wife in Corinth who had come from Italy. Acts 18:2 and Acts 18:3 say what work they shared.
c2-act-0008: A craftsman stirred up a crowd that shouted for two hours. Acts 19:24, Acts 19:27, and Acts 19:34 record their chant.
c2-act-0009: Paul reminded the leaders how hard he had worked. Acts 20:34 and Acts 20:35 close with words of Jesus.
c1-heb-0001: This chapter starts by describing faith in one sentence. Read Hebrews 11:1 and think it over.
c1-heb-0002: One man in this chapter never faced death. Hebrews 11:5 identifies him.
c2-heb-0001: Jesus knows what it is like to be tempted. Hebrews 4:15 and Hebrews 4:16 explain how to come to God's throne.
c2-heb-0002: Abraham packed up and left when God called. Hebrews 11:8 has one more detail to notice.
c2-heb-0003: Moses chose a hard road with God's people. Hebrews 11:24 and Hebrews 11:25 say what he gave up.
c2-heb-0004: Racers get tired, but this letter cheers them on. Hebrews 12:12 and Hebrews 12:13 say what to strengthen.
c2-heb-0005: These people lived like visitors, always on the move. Hebrews 11:13 and Hebrews 11:16 say what they wished for.
c2-heb-0006: Picture a big race with a crowd cheering from the sides. Hebrews 12:1 and Hebrews 12:2 call Jesus by a special title.
c1-rev-0001: John was away from his friends when the visions began. Revelation 1:9 names where he was.
c1-rev-0002: John fell down, and a hand touched him. Jesus speaks to him in Revelation 1:17.
c2-rev-0002: The church in Ephesus tested some visitors who claimed to be apostles. Revelation 2:2 reports what they found.
c2-rev-0003: Hard days were coming for the church in Smyrna. Read Revelation 2:10 and see what Jesus offered.
c2-rev-0004: Hidden manna was waiting for the overcomers in Pergamos. Revelation 2:17 adds a second gift.
c2-rev-0005: The church in Philadelphia had only a little strength. Read Revelation 3:8 for what Jesus set before them.
c2-rev-0006: Jesus had sharp words for the church in Sardis. Revelation 3:1 and Revelation 3:2 give His instruction.
c2-rev-0007: The church in Laodicea was neither cold nor hot. Revelation 3:15, Revelation 3:16, and Revelation 3:17 let us hear how they saw themselves.
c1-rev-0003: A voice like a trumpet called John to come up. Revelation 4:1 describes what stood before him.
c1-rev-0004: John saw a throne in heaven with Someone seated on it. Read Revelation 4:2 and Revelation 4:3 to see what was around it.
c2-rev-0008: Day and night, the living creatures never stop singing. Revelation 4:8 lets us join their song.
c2-rev-0009: The twenty-four elders bow low before the throne. Revelation 4:10 and Revelation 4:11 give their reason.
c2-rev-0010: Harps in hand and golden bowls held high, the elders fall down. Revelation 5:8 explains what fills the bowls.
c2-rev-0011: One of the elders told John to look up. Revelation 5:6 and Revelation 5:7 say what stood by the throne.
c2-rev-0012: No one could be found to take the scroll, and John was very sad. Revelation 5:4 and Revelation 5:9 sing the reason in their song.
c2-rev-0013: Every creature everywhere joined one huge song of praise. Revelation 5:12, Revelation 5:13, and Revelation 5:14 bring it to a close.
c1-rev-0005: The old heaven and earth passed away in John's vision. Revelation 21:1 notes what was gone.
c1-rev-0006: A city came down from heaven, dressed like a bride. Revelation 21:2 gives its name.
c2-rev-0014: A loud voice rang out from heaven. Revelation 21:3 and Revelation 21:4 say what God will wipe away.
c2-rev-0015: It is done, said the One on the throne. Revelation 21:6 has what He said next.
c2-rev-0016: John walked through the city in his vision and noticed something missing. Revelation 21:22 says what it was.
c2-rev-0017: A clear river flows from the throne through the city. Revelation 22:1 and Revelation 22:2 say what its leaves are for.
c2-rev-0018: No sun, no moon, and no lamp in that city. Revelation 21:23 and Revelation 22:5 say who takes their place.
c2-rev-0019: Old sorrows are gone, the vision says. Listen to the One on the throne in Revelation 21:4 and Revelation 21:5.
